cards.note: Already an npm bundle package (dsh.bundle.patch -> cordis.patch.yml); no .dsh-plugin manifest or repository-plugins row to convert.
package.json already declares dsh.client; no legacy dshClient field and no dsh.plugin.json exist.
dsh.client (platform web + exports ./client) is already declared, so the client-modules scan finds it; live boot manifest carries the entry.
Every consumed service is declared: host inject ['tools','connection']; client inject ['slots','locale','connection'] after this migration.
connection/slots/locale are guaranteed in the web profile this bundle enters; no optional host service is read through property access.
The plugin subscribes to no session/event stream and derives no session state from event fields.
The client half is a settings-section page; it consumes no ctx.sessions or client session API.
No task/run output tailing and no tasks.peek/read usage anywhere in the plugin.
No httpServer/tasks/onTaskDone identifiers: the host half uses the Connection service (ctx.connection.rpc.handle).
No ImageAttachmentRef, read_image use, or persisted image metadata in the plugin.
The plugin neither registers, wraps, parses, nor snapshot-tests read_image.
No custom DeepSeek LLM adapter, image request interceptor, or attachment/upload cache.

Removed api-proxy result type retargeted to the Connection contract: ConnectionRpcResult from @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-connection (host) and /client (browser); dead dependency/peer/meta entries deleted.
Target is alpha.2, not alpha.1, and the plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents.
No host-source patches and no imports from internal session-view paths.
No launcher wrapper, SDK/ACP integration, or direct profile-file reading; install is the ordinary dsh plugin --profile add path.
No headless wrapper or stdout/stderr parsing in the plugin.
The plugin does not set the tools presentation mode or use PTC presets/dispatch identifiers.
No permission/approval/WebFetch policy or preset composition in the plugin.

The custom RPC channel rides the official Connection seam (ctx.connection.rpc.handle), which mounts it behind requestRejection; live probe: unauthenticated POST 401, cookie-authenticated POST returns the documented result. No token handling in plugin code.
The plugin is not a model provider and registers no provider login configuration.
No third-party language registration and no custom i18n patch; the client half consumes the public ctx.locale service only.
No subagent orchestration or selector surface.
Deployment-level privacy behavior of the official DeepSeek adapter; plugin code needs no change and this fixture is not a deployment.
No PowerShell/Bash or Windows directory-picker compatibility workarounds to retire.
session-log-deepseek is not mounted or considered by this plugin.
The repository ships no browser acceptance script or wrapper that hardcodes the web root URL, bundle path, or log format.
No structured-question answerer registration.
No agent-preset inference from persisted sessions and no agent-presets roots.
No isTokenDelta/TPS computation.
The bundle patch only inserts its own row; it does not restate dsh-base telemetry or package-inventory rows.
No direct @earendil-works/pi-ai dependency or import.
Removed client-runtime context type replaced by @deepseek-ai/cordis Context; the package is gone from dsh.client.inject, peerDependencies and peerDependenciesMeta.

Assembly row name and live boot-manifest id both equal package.json#name; the source records that the emitted client artifact must register under that same id (the fixture ships source, so the built bundle is a release-build item, see report section 4).
The client half reads no session timeline or user message content; it only calls the plugin's own RPC channel.
No composer DOM manipulation (draft injection, history recall, selection operations).
No MarkdownText or fenced CodeBlock rendering in the plugin.
The client consumes the surviving ctx.connection.rpc.call face; it never used the removed ctx.connection.api/history/transcript surface.
No subagent seed/persisted descriptors or subagent/descriptor assertions.
No workspaces navigation/directory-picker calls (connectWorkspace/startSession/pickDirectory/listDirectory/createDirectory).
The plugin produces no third-party persisted SessionEvents and ships no persistence/reload/transport seam.
No ctx.remote usage: the plugin handles the Connection ConnectionRpcResult envelope, whose error.code is an open string and whose plugin-owned 'internal' vocabulary is unchanged.

Dead dependency/peer edges removed, @deepseek-ai/cordis floor set to ^4.0.1, ui-renderer peer added for the slots type merge; every named @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peer is published at 0.1.2-alpha.2 and its range admits it (npm view).
No Node-version workaround or startup wrapper in the repository; verification ran on Node 24.21, outside the failure window.
The plugin does not consume pluginInventory/list or validate PluginInventorySnapshot.
No host.describe or ctx.remote.$host usage; the settings page reaches the host through its own RPC channel.

The plugin lists only @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools as a host peer (its inject is ['systemPrompt'], no sessionProjections), and it installs into the shipped web profile whose base layer mounts session-projection.
The plugin never imports @deepseek-ai/dsh-settings and registers no settings namespace; its config travels over its own RPC channel.
